axes.model_access: Digital-human video lines: Avatar, Voice (dubbing/cloning) and Translation (video translation and lip-sync). Official pages do not disclose model-by-model versions; check the product capability table and API docs (2026-11-21).
axes.runtime: Web (heygen.com) plus API (developers.heygen.com); generation runs in the vendor cloud, and the API returns a video_id for an asynchronous job that the client polls or receives via webhook. No model runs locally (2026-11-21).
axes.local_files: Works live in the account cloud, with generation history visible on the web works page. Download URLs from the API expire after seven days and must be retrieved within that window; downloads then belong to the local machine. The official FAQ says 100% of user data is not used for model training (2026-11-21).
axes.background: Generation queues asynchronously in the cloud: the API returns a video_id, and the client polls status or receives webhooks, so jobs do not depend on the local machine being online. Official pages offer no pause/resume queue panel; batch production is orchestrated through the API state machine (2026-11-21).
axes.tools: An avatar library plus real-person cloning (consent-gated), voice cloning, video translation with lip-sync, Interactive Avatar Streaming API, Template API and webhook events. The official API docs list Avatar, Photo Avatar, Video Translate, Streaming and Templates separately (2026-11-21).
axes.context: Work is organised by project or brand space, and avatar assets provide cross-video consistency and context. The official FAQ and product pages list no conversational cross-session memory; scripts and templates carry the context (2026-11-21).
axes.permissions: Accounts, subscriptions and enterprise tiers. The official product page says every custom avatar must pass an on-camera identity verification by the person, without which no avatar can be created, and HeyGen honours removal requests. The FAQ says consent, avatar-usage and content guidelines are strictly enforced, and 100% of user data is not used for training (2026-11-21).
axes.fit: Fit: enterprise training/marketing localisation through translation and lip-sync, authorised real-person clones and batch talking-head video. Not fit: creative narrative generation, entertainment with a deliberately AI look, or cloning someone without consent (a terms red line) (2026-11-21).

runs: This entry checks the official site, FAQ and API docs for capability and consent boundaries. Lip-sync quality, verification strictness and batch-render behaviour need account-level measurement.
unknowns:
- Underlying generation models: not disclosed model by model; check the product capability table.
- Product scope of the Interactive Avatar Streaming API: check the official API docs.
- Training-use controls: the FAQ says user data is not used for training; enterprise data terms follow the contract.
- Mainland compliance entry: official pages list no service entry for the mainland public.
related: The two enterprise digital-human heavyweights: Synthesia is more corporate training-oriented, HeyGen more flexible on cloning and translation.
Both digital-human talking heads: D-ID is light on photo-driven, HeyGen's product line is wider.
Another species of video generation: Runway builds visuals, HeyGen builds "people talking".
API downstream: HeyGen's API often reaches content pipelines through Zapier-style platforms — batch localization only scales that way.
